meta.title: THE BRIDGE — explore your path
meta.description: A platform that helps teenagers, students and adults explore possible paths through their own answers, real human stories and small experiments.

footer.tagline: A bridge between the questions of young people and the experience of those who have already found their path.

hero.title: Your future doesn't have to be figured out today.
hero.lead: Explore who you could become through your own answers, real human stories and small experiments — without pressure or ready-made answers.
hero.note: You can start right away, no sign-up needed.
hero.todayText: who you are: interests, questions, doubts

problem.title: Paths are often chosen at random.
problem.lead: At 16 or 17 you are expected to make a decision that feels final. Few people get the chance to understand themselves or try anything in practice first.
problem.p1Text: A major is picked before you know what you actually enjoy.
problem.p2Text: You only see a handful of familiar jobs, and real human stories are scarce.
problem.p3Text: Family expectations and fear of mistakes drown out your own interests.

stats.title: You are not the only one who doesn't know yet.
stats.graduatesText: More than 30% of graduates in Kazakhstan work outside their field of study.

how.title: Four steps you can take at your own pace.
how.step1Text: Answer questions about your interests, values and what gives you energy.
how.step2Text: Read the stories of people who started with similar questions.
how.step3Text: Get a breakdown of which directions are worth exploring and why — no verdicts.
how.step4Text: Run a small experiment and test an interest in practice.

stories.title: Paths are rarely straight.
stories.lead: Stories of people who changed direction, doubted and found their own way. Every story is labelled with where it comes from — we never pass off examples as real lives.
stories.kindsLabel: Every story carries one of three labels:
stories.verifiedDesc: The source has been checked via a link.
stories.documentedDesc: Told publicly — in an interview, book or article.
stories.userDesc: Sent by a community member and reviewed by moderators.
stories.demoDesc: A fictional example that shows how the platform works.

try.title: A small experiment beats endless doubt.
try.lead: Short tasks that let you feel a profession from the inside in one evening, not four years of study.
try.example2: Work through a real case like a lawyer

community.lead: THE BRIDGE is an educational project run by a team of ambassadors. We build a bridge between the questions of young people and the experience of those who have already found their path.

explore.completeLead: You have covered the essentials. Now you can build your personal report — not a verdict and not a prediction, but a map of directions worth exploring.
explore.missingTitle: A few more questions to go
explore.missingLead: Without these blocks the report would be too vague:

A1.title: How old are you?
A1.hint: Pick a range — an exact age is not needed.
A1.whyWeAsk: Age changes which questions and examples help most: a school student and someone changing careers face different choices.

A2.title: What are you doing right now?
A2.whyWeAsk: So we do not ask too much: a school student does not need questions about jobs, and someone working does not need questions about choosing a school.

options.other: Something else (a pause, searching, parental leave…)

A3.title: Which country and city are you from?
A3.hint: Optional. You can write only the country, or skip.
A3.whyWeAsk: Opportunities and scholarships often depend on the country. This is only used to suggest options that fit.

A4.title: What are you studying, and how is it going?
A4.hint: Write your field and a few words on whether you like it. Optional.

A5.title: What are you doing at the moment?
A5.hint: A job, a side job, a pause — whatever is true. Optional.

A6.title: How clear is your idea of what to do after school?
A6.hint: An honest answer beats a “right” one.

options.some: I have a couple of options but I am not sure
options.pause: I want to pause first and look around

B1.title: What draws you in?
B1.hint: Pick up to five topics or activities. There are no wrong answers.
B1.whyWeAsk: This is the basis for ideas and experiments. Choose what resonates, not what you “should” choose.

options.unsure: Not sure yet — a bit of everything

B2.title: What could you talk about for hours, or what do you teach yourself?
B2.hint: Topics, channels, books, hobbies — anything that comes to mind.

B3.title: What absorbs you so much that you lose track of time?
B3.hint: Any activity, even if it feels unserious.

B4.title: What would you do if nothing limited you — money, other people's expectations, fear?
B4.hint: Dream a little. You can be bolder here than usual.

C1.title: Are you more comfortable working alone or in a team?
C1.hint: Pick 1 to 5 for what is closer. There are no right answers.
C1.whyWeAsk: This is not a grade or a label, just a hint about which working environment might suit you.

C2.title: How much do you enjoy talking with lots of people at work?

C3.title: What is closer to you: practice or theory?
C3.whyWeAsk: It helps us pick experiments in a format that suits you. Not a label, just a guide.

C4.title: How do you feel when a task is hard and there are no clear instructions?
C4.scaleMax: I enjoy figuring it out myself

C5.title: What matters more to you in work: stability or experimenting?
C5.whyWeAsk: So we understand which directions and first steps feel comfortable, and which are too risky for you right now.

D1.title: Which of these have you already done?
D1.hint: You can pick several. If none yet, that is perfectly fine.

D2.title: Tell us about one such experience: what did you do, and what are you proud of?
D2.hint: A couple of sentences is enough.

D3.title: Was there an experience that changed how you see something, or a difficulty you overcame?
D3.hint: Optional, but stories like these say a lot about you.

E1.title: What is hardest for you about choosing a path?
E1.whyWeAsk: So the advice reflects what actually gets in the way, not just a list of professions.

options.noIdea: I do not know what I like
options.wrongChoice: I am afraid of choosing wrong
options.noTalent: I feel I have no special talent
options.tooLate: I feel it is already too late

E2.title: Do you feel pressure from your family about your path?
E2.whyWeAsk: This is personal. We ask so we do not give advice that is hard to use at home.

E2b.title: How does it show up?
E2b.hint: Pick the closest one. You can skip this.
E2b.whyWeAsk: This is also personal. Answer only if you want to — it helps us see which steps are realistic.

options.profession: They want me to pick a specific profession
options.closeToHome: They want me to stay close to home
options.income: They expect me to start earning soon

E3.title: Have you already chosen something that now feels like it is not yours?
E3.hint: A major, a university, a job — anything.

E3b.title: What exactly does not fit?
E3b.hint: What does not resonate, and maybe what you still like about it?

E4.title: Do you sometimes feel you have no particular talent?
E4.hint: There is no right answer — many people feel this way.

F1.title: What matters most to you in your future work and life?
F1.whyWeAsk: Values help find a path that fits you, not “everyone”.

F2.title: What does “success” mean to you?
F2.hint: In your own words, no polished phrasing needed.

F3.title: What problems in the world or around you would you like to solve?

F4.title: What would make your life feel meaningful?

G1.title: Are there real-life limits that affect your choice?
G1.hint: Optional. Pick up to three that matter most.
G1.whyWeAsk: To suggest realistic steps and opportunities, such as scholarships. You can skip this.

G2.title: How are you placed for paying for study?
G2.whyWeAsk: So we understand whether scholarships and grants matter for you. It only affects the suggestions.

options.selfFunded: I can pay, or my family can help
options.partial: I can cover part of it
options.needScholarship: I need a scholarship or grant

G3.title: How easy is access to education where you live?
G3.whyWeAsk: It decides whether in-person options fit or starting online makes more sense.

G4.title: Which languages do you speak?
G4.hint: You can pick several. You can skip this.
G4.whyWeAsk: Language affects study and work opportunities, including abroad.

G5.title: How much time per week can you give to something new?
G5.whyWeAsk: So experiments and the plan are doable, not one more source of stress.

G6.title: How willing are you to move?
G6.whyWeAsk: Study options and opportunities depend on it.

options.city: I need to stay in my city

G7.title: What family responsibilities do you have?
G7.whyWeAsk: So the steps are realistic and do not need more time than you have.

options.some: Some, but I still have time
options.main: They take most of my time

try.philosophy: You do not have to choose your whole future today. You can try first.

section.obstacles: What may get in the way

mentors.title: Ask a human
mentors.lead: THE BRIDGE plans to connect people who are looking for their path with volunteers and experienced professionals who are ready to share their experience.
mentors.statusTitle: For now these are only plans.
mentors.statusLead: There are no mentors on the platform yet, and we don't show made-up profiles. Leave your interest and message us, and we'll find someone to talk to.
mentors.plan1: A mentor does not decide for you: they share their path and answer questions.
mentors.plan2: Taking part is voluntary, with no obligations for you or for the mentor.
mentors.plan3: We will try to match topics and experience, not promise a specific result.
mentors.formLead: Choose who you would like to be. It takes a couple of minutes.

about.title: A bridge between questions and experience
about.lead: THE BRIDGE is an educational project. We build a bridge between the questions of young people and the experience of those who have already found their path.
about.mission: We do not choose the future for people. We help them see that there are more possibilities than it seemed.
about.what1: A questionnaire that helps you notice patterns in your answers and builds a report without verdicts.
about.what2: People’s stories. Each one is labelled: verified source, publicly documented with a link to the original, or from a user.
about.what3: Small experiments to feel a direction before you choose it.
about.what4: Programmes, scholarships and internships with official links and the date of the last check.
about.freeText: You do not pay to use the platform.
about.noAdsText: There is no advertising on the pages.
about.noPaidText: Stories, opportunities and directions do not get into the lists for money.
about.founderNote: The name and role are given as they are signed on the project’s certificate.
about.certificateAlt: THE BRIDGE certificate (Certificate of Appreciation) signed by Aidyn Kaldykara, Founder & Project Leader, with the “Ambassadors of the Earth” stamp
about.certificateCaption: A THE BRIDGE certificate with the founder’s signature and the “Ambassadors of the Earth” stamp.

privacy.title: What we do with your data
privacy.lead: Short and in plain words: what is stored, where, what goes to the AI, and how to download or delete it all.
privacy.where1: While no database is connected, everything is stored only in your browser: questionnaire answers, reports, plan, journal, saved items, experiments, the mentor request and settings. We do not keep this data ourselves. The project’s server receives your answers only when you ask for a report or a scenario, processes them and does not store them.
privacy.where2: If a database is connected and you are signed in, the questionnaire, reports, plan, journal, saved items, experiments and settings are kept in the database. The exception: the mentor request and experiments you have started but not finished stay only in this browser. By the access rules each record in the database is visible only to its owner.
privacy.where3: If the browser does not allow storage (for example in private mode), data lives only until you close the tab. The pages warn you about it.
privacy.where4: A story you send for publication goes to the database. The team reviews it, and it is shown only after the review. You choose whether to give your name. If you delete your data in Settings, a story that is still waiting for review is deleted. Only the team can remove a story that is already published.
privacy.aiTitle: What goes to the AI service
privacy.ai1: Data goes to the AI service only when AI is connected on the project’s server. For the report that is your questionnaire answers, for the chat your messages, and for the “What if I try?” scenario the chosen direction, your note and the questionnaire answers, if you have them.
privacy.ai2: Whatever you write in your own words is passed to the model as data, not as commands, and markup is removed from the text.
privacy.ai3: The journal, saved stories and opportunities, experiments and plans are not sent to the AI service.
privacy.ai4: If AI is not connected, demo mode works: reports and scenarios are built by rules on the project’s server and nothing goes to outside services. A label on the screen tells you so.
privacy.memory1: Memory is off by default. You can turn it on or off in the chat and in the settings.
privacy.memory2: If you turn it on, the conversation is saved and the AI sees a short summary of your questionnaire answers so it does not ask again. If you turn it off, the saved conversation is erased.
privacy.memory3: Even with memory off, your message goes to the AI service the moment you send it: otherwise there would be no answer. It just is not kept anywhere once you close the page.
privacy.yours1: In the settings you can download all your data as one file (JSON).
privacy.yours2: You can also delete your data there. It takes two confirmations so you do not erase everything by accident. The data cannot be restored afterwards.
privacy.ads1: We do not show ads and we do not take money for recommendations.
privacy.ads2: We do not sell your data and do not use it for advertising. It is received only by the project’s database and, when it is connected, by the AI service in the cases described above.
privacy.limits1: This is a plain-language description, not a legal document. We make no claims in it about compliance with specific laws.
privacy.limits2: If anything changes in what we send and where, this page will change with it.
privacy.yours3: If you are signed in, the data in the account and in the browser, your stories that are still waiting for review, and the name on your profile are deleted. These stay: stories the team has already reviewed (published or rejected), reports you sent about stories, and the account itself. The project team deletes them.
privacy.where5: The site counts anonymously how many people visit, start and finish the questionnaire and get a report: only the action's name and the page language, no names and no texts. So one person isn't counted twice a day, the browser keeps the date of the last count.
privacy.ai5: The site's AI currently runs on Google Gemini (the Gemini API). The chat, the report and the “What if I try?” scenario send it the text described below.
privacy.ai6: The project uses the free tier of the Gemini API. Under Google's terms, on the free tier Google may use prompts and answers to improve its products, and human reviewers may read them (detached from the account). So don't write your name, phone number, address, ID number or other personal details in the chat.

auth.title: Sign in to THE BRIDGE
auth.lead: Signing in is optional: every page works without an account. You only need it to continue on another phone or computer.
auth.guestText: As a guest you can take the questionnaire, get a report, and keep a journal and a plan. Everything is stored on this device, in this browser.
auth.syncText: When you sign in, your data syncs across devices: start on your phone, continue on your computer. Only you can see your private answers, reports and journal.

setup.title: The admin panel will work once Supabase is set up
setup.lead: The site currently runs without a database, so signing in and managing content is not possible. Here is what to do, once.
setup.step1Text: Sign up at supabase.com and create a new project.
setup.step2Text: Run the files in the supabase/migrations folder in order (0001, 0002, 0003, 0004, 0005): with the Supabase CLI command supabase db push, or by pasting them into the SQL editor.
setup.step3Text: Add the project URL and keys to .env.local, then restart the site. The service role key is used only on the server and never reaches the browser.
setup.step4Text: Sign in to the site with the emailed link, find your user id in Supabase (Authentication, Users) and run the command below in the SQL editor with your id filled in.
setup.note: After that, an "Administration" item appears in your account menu.

stories.title: Story moderation
stories.lead: Stories sent in by people. Read each one in full, choose a type, then publish or reject it. The types "documented" and "verified" need a source link.

stories.kindHelp: "User submitted" needs no source. "Publicly documented" and "Verified source" need an http or https link.
stories.sourceNameHelp: For user stories the author's name is not changed.
stories.noteHelp: Visible to the team only. Do not write personal data.

reports.lead: Open reports about stories. Check the story and close the report: resolved or dismissed.
